end_to_end.actual: All checks exit 0. AC#2's largest error was 0.957 pp (hu-064). The generator wrote 121 cases in about 30 s and git diff exit 0 (byte-identical). p95 at scale 1: 5.78/0.19/5.12/6.42/8.17/21.26/69.62 ms against targets 15/2/20/15/20/50/80, all pass. Mutation probes: counting a tie as a full win failed AC#1, AC#2, AC#3 and the SPEC-07 test. Seeding from Date.now failed AC#4 and AC#5. Dropping the board sort failed AC#4 and AC#5. Lowering the exact limit to 190,000 failed the SPEC-08 test.

The diff against 99b1c4c touches no existing src/engine or src/ui file and no existing test. items.evidence: AC#1 passes locally and on CI. The test asserts method 'sampled', trials 30000, both equities within 0.015 of the published values and a sum within 1e-12. The tie-as-win mutation makes it fail.

AC#2 passes locally: 120 HU matchups, largest error 0.957 pp, 4137 ms. The test asserts at least 100 cases, distinct unordered pairs and a 0.015 bound for both players, and the tie-as-win mutation fails it (hu-008 off by 2.19 pp). Holdout: sampled HU 22 vs AKs (not in the fixture) is within 0.114 pp of an independent exhaustive enumeration. Caveat: on CI the same test hit Vitest's 5000 ms default timeout (finding J-1-01, filed under SPEC-15).

The equity-reference test passes and checks trials, win+tie <= trials, the share-unit sums, 6-decimal rounding, ids and players equal to REFERENCE_MATCHUPS, the section 5 rule 6 anchors, and an exact re-enumeration of hu-002 and hu-004. Independently, a full `node tools/equity/generate-reference.js` regenerated a byte-identical fixture.

AC#3 passes: sampled, all three equities within 0.015 of mw-001, sum within 1e-12. Holdout: three-way preflop JJ vs AKo vs 76s (not in the fixture) is sampled and within 0.266 pp of independent exhaustive enumeration.

AC#4 passes, including the spawned fresh node process. Holdout: two new inputs (a 4-player preflop with a range, and a 3-way flop with full ranges) gave the same result digest 8108f8b2 in two separate fresh processes. Swapping two distinct opponents on a sampled input maps the results back exactly. The Date.now-seed and unsorted-board mutations both make AC#4 fail.

AC#5 passes: Math.random is stubbed, fake timers are set to 2001 and 2030, seed equality and inequality are checked, and banned tokens are scanned for. Holdout: deriveSeed equals fnv1a32(canonicalKey) on a multi-opponent board input. The Date.now-seed mutation makes AC#5 fail.

The unit test passes with exact equality on 85/990 and 905/990, the river chop, the generator cross-check and the three-way royal chop at 1/3. Holdout: four exact cases (flop HU, 3-way turn, 4-way river with ranges, turn hand vs 1,035-combo range) match an independent enumerator in trials, win, tie and equity to 1e-9.

The unit test passes: six estimates (river case 1,980 per A-12) plus the 191,646 exact / 201,600 sampled boundary. The 190k-limit mutation fails it. Holdout: a 3-way flop at estimate 172,200 chose exact and a larger range chose sampled, both as the rule predicts.

The unit test passes: dead and duplicate combos removed, fast-check permutations with numRuns 50, the key example, and one live combo equal to hand vs hand. Holdout: canonicalKey for hero Kh As, board 2c Td 3s and two opponents is 'equity-v1|h:46,51|b:0,7,33|o:25,29/36,39;41,42' with order [1,0], as the section 5 rule 2 requires. The input object is not mutated.

The unit test passes with every listed message, the rejection cap at 0 and the default-cap success (opponent 1 always gets QhQc). Holdout: 21 further error cases all throw RangeError with the exact message. They cover hero with 0 or 3 cards, board with 1 or 6 cards, validation order (hero, then board, then opponent count, then cards), cards -1, 1.5, NaN and '5', board card 52, duplicates in hero and in board, one-card combo ('5,undefined'), opponent 3 combo 0,52, empty range, a range emptied by hero cards, and cannot-deal for an exact 3-way flop and a 9-opponent preflop. Nine opponents are accepted.
The perf test passes locally with coverage (worst 351 ms against 1600 ms) and passed on CI (589.6 ms against 1600 ms). It asserts the method for each scenario and p95 <= target x scale.
`EQUITY_PERF_SCALE=1 npx vitest run tests/advice/equity.perf.test.ts` on arm64 macOS with Node v22.18.0 passed 1 test. Full-ring p95 was 69.62 ms against the 80 ms target (closest margin).

The unit test passes with all vectors. Holdout: the xoshiro128** published vector from state 1,2,3,4 matches. FNV-1a 'hello' = 0x4f9f2cab matches the published value. A chi-square on 520,000 nextInt(52) draws gave 46.1 (df 51), and the bit-balance z-score was -2.03.
lint, typecheck and npm test all exit 0 with no ERROR: Coverage line. equity.ts has 100% lines and seeded-random.ts 100% lines (checked separately). The grep pipeline prints nothing (exit 0).

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected: CI on doit/TASK-7.1 concludes success. Actual: run 44231570428 (51eddcb) failed because the locked AC#2 test (120 sampled heads-up computeEquity calls, no explicit timeout) exceeded Vitest's default 5000 ms per-test timeout on the CI runner with coverage. Locally it takes about 4.1 s, only about 17% headroom.
findings.fix: AC#2 must finish well inside the 5 s per-test timeout on the CI runner with coverage, without editing the locked acceptance test. Either make 120 heads-up preflop sampled computeEquity calls substantially faster (for example, remove the per-trial allocations in the sampler's hot loop), or, if the orchestrator approves it as a deviation, raise the per-test timeout in the test configuration. Then push and get a green CI run.

summary: 15 of 16 SPEC items are verified locally and with independent holdout checks: exact cases match an independent enumerator exactly, sampled cases are within 0.27 pp of independent exhaustive values (including heavy-overlap ranges that exercise whole-deal rejection), results are deterministic across fresh processes, and all errors are exact. The end-to-end run passes: the fixture regenerates byte-identical, reference-machine perf meets every target, and all four mutation probes are caught. Integrity is clean.
